title: Working into a chain space
subtitle: Insert under the chain arch, not into a specific chain stitch
excerpt: Working into a chain space means inserting the hook under the entire chain arch — through the open gap below all the chains — rather than into one individual chain stitch. This is the standard method for granny squares, lace patterns, V-stitches, and any pattern with ch-2 or longer spaces between stitches.

glossaryTerms.definition: The open arch formed by one or more chains skipped over in the previous row. Working into a chain space inserts the hook under all the chains of the arch at once — not into any individual chain stitch. Abbreviated ch sp or ch-2 sp (for a two-chain space).

heroPrompt: Close-up of a hook inserted under a chain space arch — under all three chains at once — with a granny square motif visible in the background, showing the hook path clearly.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Hook inserted under a ch-3 arch, passing under all three chains with hook tip emerging through the open space below

content.text: insertions look simple but trip up many beginners because the written instruction 'work into ch-3 sp' does not mean 'insert into one of the chains.' It means insert the hook through the open gap below all three chains — under the arch, not into it. When you insert under the whole arch, the new stitch sits neatly in the opening and uses all the chains as its base.
Locate the chain space — the open gap formed by 2, 3, or more chain stitches from the row below.
Hold the chain arch slightly open with the left thumb. Insert the hook from front to back through the gap below all the chains — the hook passes under all of them at once.
Work the stitch normally (dc, tr, etc.). The completed stitch encloses the chain arch inside its body.

attrs.title: When the pattern says 'into the 2nd chain'
attrs.body: Some patterns do specify inserting into individual chain stitches — for example, 'dc into 2nd ch from hook' when starting a foundation row. This is different from working into a chain space. Read the instruction: 'ch sp' or 'ch-2 sp' = under the arch. '2nd chain' or 'ch 4' = into a specific chain stitch.

items.symptom: Stitches look uneven — some sit on top of the chain, some under it
items.cause: Inconsistently inserting into single chain stitches on some passes and under the arch on others
items.fix: Always insert under the entire arch for chain-space stitches. Hold the arch open with the left hand so the gap is visible before inserting.

content.text: Working into a chain space is used in nearly every lace and motif pattern: granny squares, V-stitch, shell, fan, and filet mesh all rely on this insertion method. It is also the basis of working around the post of a stitch (FPDC/BPDC), where the hook goes under the post — a comparable under-the-structure insertion.
